web.title: Glenigan reviews, one and two stars (Trustpilot)
Wachtlijst netcongestie groeit naar ruim 15.000 bedrijven

summary: Sixteen supplier calls between 7 and 23 September tested the pitch in venture.md, which project to call and why now, and the answer was mostly no: five commercial leads said finding projects is not their problem, and two said the paid project databases they know arrive late or cost too much. The E4 pains sit after the lead: only a tenth to a quarter of requests are worth pursuing, finding who holds the budget takes hours per lead, and reps spend much of the week asking architects whether the product is still specified. From 23 September the calls moved to estimators at facade subcontractors, a different buyer with strong E4 pains on unreadable tender packages and drawings that contradict the specification, but no pilot or price yet. The two journeys meet at one step: reading the tender documents to find what a party would actually supply.

icps.name: Commercial lead at a building-product supplier
icps.segment: Makers and distributors of specified building products (facade panels, cladding, profiles, facade PV, bio-based materials), about 8 to 60 staff, Netherlands and Benelux
icps.who: Account managers, business developers and front-end specification sellers who work architects early and hand a project to colleagues once the contractor is known.
icps.trigger: A sample request, platform enquiry or tender lands and they must decide quickly whether it is real, big enough and reachable at the person who pays.
jobs: Separate the few real, large enough projects from the inbound pile
Find who decides and funds, not only the junior who asked
Keep track of where each project stands over a one to two year cycle
Get the product into the specification before it closes
icps.notes: E4 pains from four suppliers on triage, decision-makers and status chasing, and one E5 request to be a test user. Five of sixteen supplier calls said more leads is not their problem. Energy-storage sellers were interviewed too and fit worse: the strongest grid signal is a private conversation with the grid operator.

icps.name: Estimator at a facade or envelope subcontractor
icps.segment: Facade cladding, steel and metalwork subcontractors and general contractors, about 30 to 100 staff with one to seven estimators, Netherlands
icps.who: Calculators, work planners and commercial directors who turn a tender package of drawings and specification into a priced quote that can actually be built.
icps.trigger: A tender package arrives with a fixed submission date, or the only full-time calculator is about to retire.
jobs: Filter a tender package down to the firm's own scope
Reconcile specification, drawings and details before pricing
Derive every component and the labour, not only the square metres
Get a complete quote out before the deadline
icps.notes: Eleven calls in three days, 23 to 25 September, after the venture moved its discovery to calculation. E4 pains are consistent across firms, but nobody has committed to a pilot or price, two firms already work with other AI builders and one has turned down two vendor pitches.

journeys.title: From a request to a project the supplier is specified on
journeys.question: Can Modou keep the state of the projects a supplier already has (real, budget holder, phase, what it would supply) so the team stops chasing and starts at the right person?

asis.text: Most projects arrive inbound: sample requests, download forms, architects who know the brand
Paid feeds such as Cobouw, Mercuur and tender calendars are scanned by hand, if anyone still does it

decisions.title: Stop pitching project discovery; sell the state of projects the supplier already has
decisions.why: Five supplier calls said lead supply is not the problem, while E4 pains sit in triage, finding the budget holder and chasing status. It also matches the 19 and 22 September decisions to sell memory and knowledge of state.

decisions.title: Build the tender and request reader first, because both buyers need it
decisions.why: Suppliers skip tender requests they cannot read and estimators spend days filtering packages. One engine serves both, which lets the evidence choose the buyer.

decisions.title: Do not price labour or build an estimating engine
decisions.why: Estimators say the experience behind labour, cranes and access does not transfer to software, incumbents such as IBIS and Admicom hold the calculation, and two vendor pitches already failed at one firm.

decisions.title: Treat the budget holder as a hypothesis, tested on the pilot's 20 to 50 projects
decisions.why: It is the top supplier pain, but one supplier said it cannot be automated and nobody has checked whether public documents name the funder of private projects.

decisions.title: Leave energy storage out of the first ICP
decisions.why: The strongest grid signal is a private talk with the grid operator, congestion leads are a price fight, and one buyer's boss calls project data nonsense.

decisions.title: Ask every pilot for a price before 4 December
decisions.why: No one has named a price for Modou. The references heard are a recalled 2,000 euros a month for Mercuur, 4,360 euros a year quoted for Cobouw, a 5,000 euro self-approval limit and 60 euro DIY bots.
